story: Gary is out on Magnolia Loop in the breezy 74-degree morning, hopeful about getting his golf cart approved, while Donna stands nearby with a packed bag of extra paddles and an invitation to pickleball at one o'clock. Hal, mellow as ever, offers to help Gary haul a box of porch lights to the curb after lunch, promising to supervise every step. Meanwhile, Rosa is in her kitchen with her sleeves rolled up, determined to finish bagging the baked treats for tomorrow's trick-or-treaters.
events: Rosa (rosa kitchen): Finish packing the baked treats into bags for tomorrow's trick-or-treaters

gary.thought_process: Donna just arrived and Hal already got his say. Parade is tomorrow, application still isn't signed off, and Rosa is supposed to be bringing my sketches over to the review desk. I've already asked Hal if he needs help, so I shouldn't repeat that. Donna invited me to the courts earlier, so a friendly word to her fits, and I can mention that I'm waiting on the committee but glad to have her and Rosa in my corner. Keep it short and honest, no cart work until approval.

parameters.content: Morning, Donna. Still waiting on the committee to sign off on the cart, so I'm keeping my hands to myself till then. Is that courts invitation still good for later, or are you tied up with the parade prep?

donna.thought_process: Gary and Hal are both right here on Magnolia Loop. Last I heard, Gary and I were on for third-shot drop drills tomorrow, and I just packed extra paddles and balls, but tomorrow is also Halloween parade day, so I should lock in a time instead of hoping. Gary is the one I need for the ladder climb, so I'll talk to him directly and get a concrete time on the court. I won't repeat the flamingo chat from before; this line moves things forward.

parameters.content: Gary! Bag's packed with extra paddles. Let's hit the courts at 1 for third-shot drops, and we'll be done well before the parade tomorrow. You in?

hal.thought_process: Gary already answered me and offered help. I've said my piece on the cart, and he's doing what I asked. Donna just arrived, and I've already warned her directly about the flamingos. The decent thing now is to be neighborly, not file a complaint before the committee rules. Gary asked if I need help before tomorrow's parade, so I'll answer him plainly and briefly, then let things be. Don't repeat the cart business.

parameters.content: Matter of fact, Gary, I've got a box of porch lights in the garage that need hauling to the curb for the parade. Stop by after lunch and I'll stand over you and supervise.

rosa.thought_process: I'm at home Friday morning and the parade is tomorrow. I already checked my shift schedule and baked treats last tick, so the kitchen work is underway. Nobody is nearby, so there's no one to talk to. The best use of this hour is to keep baking so there are plenty of treats for trick-or-treaters and the parade crowd, since I want tomorrow to bring neighbors together. Cart and decor details are already settled with Gary and Donna.

parameters.content: Finish packing the baked treats into bags for tomorrow's trick-or-treaters

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
